balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For MTU Aero Engines AG: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For MTU Aero Engines AG: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For MTU Aero Engines AG: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For MTU Aero Engines AG: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Adjusted FCF is MTU's own guidance metric: it starts from reported FCF but excludes one-off cash items tied to the GTF geared-turbofan programme (customer compensation receipts/payments related to the fleet issues), so it is not directly comparable period to period with the unadjusted line. Owner FCF (from the DCF) is a separate, independent construction that further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For MTU Aero Engines AG: management guides the market to Adjusted FCF each year, so it is the number to check against guidance; the gap between net income and owner FCF is the separate earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • Adjusted FCF versus the FY guidance range given at each results call
  • A widening gap between Reported and Adjusted FCF (growing GTF one-offs)
  • FCF persistently below net income

netFinancialDebt.title: Net financial debt
netFinancialDebt.content:
Net financial debt is MTU's own disclosed figure: gross financial debt (bonds, bank loans and lease liabilities) less cash and cash equivalents. It differs from the generic Cash vs Total Debt chart because MTU's own definition nets the two together and is the figure quoted in its own reporting and covenants.

For MTU Aero Engines AG: the DCF's equity bridge uses this net financial debt figure directly (including lease liabilities as debt) to go from enterprise value to equity value, so it should be checked against the DCF JSON's net_debt input at the valuation date.

What to watch:

  • Net financial debt rising faster than EBITDA (leverage)
  • Convertible bond (EUR 500m, 2027) carried inside gross debt while out of the money
  • Spikes around aircraft-engine programme ramp-up capex or buybacks

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For MTU Aero Engines AG: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For MTU Aero Engines AG: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For MTU Aero Engines AG: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For MTU Aero Engines AG: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For MTU Aero Engines AG: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
